meta.notes: Mission Control KPIs (v2). value = P2 network positioning, the CORE finding; baseline = P0 starting-point OEM-quote provisioning (Simple Rulebook); reference = I125, the frontier option for additional capital (the rule's pick); headline = the computed site headline (core / frontier_option / honest). Holdout seeds 2000-2019, central variant, KPI weeks 104-155 annualised; ci = 95% t-interval over 20 seeds. 'selection' repeats the same numbers on selection seeds 100-119. No 'spark' field: there is no genuine time series for these KPIs, so none is exported (UI must handle a missing spark). open_exceptions is DERIVED from history week 103.

honest.routes_note: Every policy here, P0/P1/P2 included, relies on the v2 AOG-desk routes (V2-SIM-5/14, config aog_sourcing, ASSUMED): robbery at AUH (engineering/quality approval required), local borrow at outstations and exchange/loan by fleet, retried every 72 h for rotables, plus local buy for C/E; in practice this means access to an AOG exchange/loan market and to borrow agreements. Borrowed units never join the owned pool. With the routes switched off (tornado row 'aog_desk_expedite off'), expected material-related downtime rises sharply for every policy, so the frontier is conditional on those markets existing at the assumed availability.
honest.routes_line: All four plans rely on emergency sourcing (borrowing from another aircraft, loans, local purchase). With those routes switched off, every plan's downtime rises sharply — e.g. Network Plan from ≈235 h to ≈18,320 h a year (selection runs). See Limitations.

reading_note: How to read these numbers: simulated downtime of the aircraft waiting for the part, across 120 modelled part numbers. Downtime of aircraft that donated a part (cannibalisation) is shown separately, not included. The Simple Rulebook is a deliberately simplified starting point, not a model of a competent airline. Part costs, reliability and sourcing are assumed. These are not forecasts of achievable airline savings.

capital_table.note: Removed stock is not cash back — it may be redeployed, consumed, exchanged or sold at a discount.

stress_worlds.ranges_note: Likely ranges reflect simulation randomness only, not uncertainty in prices, failure rates, suppliers or contracts.

frontier_insight.text: Faster repair can beat buying spares: with 25% shorter repair time, the extra-investment option loses its clear cost advantage.
